context: Add TODO_DB_CREDENTIAL_COMMAND to _VERIFY_ENV_PROTECTED_CREDENTIALS so an explicit passthrough request is refused with the existing named-but-never-valued error. Extend the existing passthrough refusal test to cover it. Review whether any other pointer-shaped variable introduced later needs the same treatment and note the rule in the source comment: the denylist protects credentials and anything that yields one on demand, not only variables that hold a secret value.
description: PR #18 added a variable that yields a bearer token on demand, and _VERIFY_ENV_PROTECTED_CREDENTIALS in src/todo_db/tracker.py still lists only TODO_DB_AUTH_TOKEN, TODO_DB_RO_AUTH_TOKEN, TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN, and TURSO_API_TOKEN. Default-deny covers the common case because the name is absent from the safe_keys allowlist, but an operator can name it in TODO_DB_VERIFY_ENV_PASSTHROUGH and the guard will accept it. Stored verification commands on a shared hosted tracker are written by other actors, which is the trust boundary verify --run already refuses to cross without TODO_DB_ALLOW_HOSTED_VERIFY_RUN. A verification command that inherits the provider variable can execute the provider and print the token, defeating verify-env-auth-secret-boundary by passing the pointer instead of the secret. Neither the adversarial review nor the implementation caught this.

anti_patterns.dont: Fix this by widening the denylist to every variable matching a pattern
anti_patterns.why: verify-env-auth-secret-boundary evaluated and rejected a blanket denylist because it breaks legitimate unrelated passthrough

anti_patterns.dont: Treat TODO_DB_CREDENTIAL_COMMAND as harmless because it holds no secret value
anti_patterns.instead: protect anything that resolves to a credential, not only variables that contain one
anti_patterns.why: it yields a bearer token on demand, so forwarding it is equivalent to forwarding the token to anything that can run a command

preserves.behavior: Legitimate explicit passthrough of unrelated verification credentials still works; only tracker and Turso credential names and now the provider pointer are refused.
No blanket *TOKEN* or *SECRET* denylist is introduced; verify-env-auth-secret-boundary rejected that and the rejection stands.
The refusal reports variable names and never values.
verify --run against a hosted backend still refuses without TODO_DB_ALLOW_HOSTED_VERIFY_RUN.
